assumptions: All numerical enclosures are conditional on python-flint 0.9.0 and its bundled FLINT/Arb implementation; the lock file and runtime version are recorded.
A sign-changing bracket proves at least one real characteristic zero by continuity. It does not by itself prove uniqueness or exclude even-multiplicity or additional sub-bracket zeros.

The exact Bessel representation transports the lambda-zero recessive solution direction without forming an ill-conditioned fundamental matrix. The ball checks cover the declared endpoint quantities and bracket bands, not every kappa in [0,8].
The Qplus Liouville-Green comparison checks only containment by the already proved lambda-zero tail budget. It is not reused as a differentiated lambda-tail theorem.
No lambda derivative is evaluated. Endpoint F_lambda, nonzero-lambda validated transport, nonreal Weyl m data, spectral measure, rigging map and C-to-H quantum equivalence remain null.

exact_checks.statement: For x=6*pi^2*exp(Q), d_Q^2=x^2*d_x^2+x*d_x converts the lambda-zero raw-C fiber to the imaginary-order modified-Bessel equation.
The exact lambda-zero Q coefficient equals x(Q)^2-kappa^2.
Both p signs have the same lambda-zero fiber coefficient.
Differentiating at lambda=0 requires the displayed forced variational equation; this runner deliberately leaves its boundary datum and F_lambda open.

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: The exact K representation and W_Q(K,I)=1 transport the lambda-zero recessive direction without an ill-conditioned raw fundamental matrix. DLMF does not provide the emitted ball enclosures or any nonzero-lambda, spectral or RAQ conclusion.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: x=6*pi^2*exp(Q)>0, nu=i*kappa, lambda=0, the K branch is recessive at positive infinity, and the derivative and Wronskian conventions are the declared ones

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: K_(i*kappa)(x0) and its Q derivative are real and continuous in real kappa, so F(kappa) is a real continuous characteristic on every certified bracket. This supplies the real-valued hypothesis used by the intermediate value theorem only at lambda=0.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: x0=6*pi^2*exp(-4)>0 and kappa is real; K_(-nu)(x0)=K_nu(x0), while conjugation maps K_(i*kappa)(x0) to K_(-i*kappa)(x0)
theorem_guards.theorem: DLMF section 10.27 order symmetry plus complex conjugation for real positive argument

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: The certificates cover only the displayed endpoint values and five sign-changing brackets at lambda=0. A small radius alone is never counted as a proof, and uniqueness is not inferred.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: Every accepted sign uses a real lower or upper bound that excludes zero; every interval conclusion uses the full input ball; both precision tiers and exact-rational nesting are retained
theorem_guards.theorem: Arb midpoint-radius inclusion arithmetic as exposed by locked python-flint 0.9.0

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: Each bracket contains at least one real zero. This does not exclude an even number of additional roots, certify uniqueness, or prove that the five brackets exhaust kappa in [0,8].
theorem_guards.hypotheses: The real-characteristic guard establishes real continuity on real kappa, and every bracket has rigorously opposite finite endpoint signs
theorem_guards.theorem: Intermediate value theorem for the entire-in-order modified Bessel K characteristic
